services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled never checks whether the identified user has a passkey credential, so re-auth and identity-first users without passkeys still get passkey UI, which offers other accounts' passkeys that then fail with DIFFERENT_USER.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` only checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, and the caller now unconditionally runs `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` whenever a user is identified (e.g., re-authentication). The diff shows no credential check (e.g., whether `context.getUser()` actually has any WebAuthn/passkey credentials). Additionally, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(...)` to always return `false`, so `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm(...)` will not perform the “no authenticators -> return early” guard in the user-identified path and will still set up conditional-passkey UI even for users without passkeys. This behavior was avoided before because `fillContextForm` was only invoked when `context.getUser() == null`. Thus the finding describes a real behavioral defect exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:282 — reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey claims passkey UI is hidden for a user without passkeys, but it turns passkeys off for the whole realm, so the real case (passkeys on, user has none) is never tested and the test passes without checking it.

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the diff explicitly disables passkeys at the realm level (`.setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`) and the accompanying comment states this is the intended scenario: "passkeys feature enabled, but passkeys is not enabled for the realm". So it is not claiming to test "passkeys on, user has none"; it is testing "realm passkeys off". The finding misreads the test’s stated purpose/setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:53 — The new re-auth error form after a passkey failure (for example another user's passkey giving DIFFERENT_USER) is not covered by any test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` by calling `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` to alter the username/password error form during re-authentication after a passkey failure. The newly added tests cover re-authentication success paths and password failure during re-authentication (`PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey()` checks incorrect password), but none of the added tests exercise a failing passkey/conditional-UI flow (e.g., a passkey failure such as DIFFERENT_USER) and then assert the re-authentication form attributes are correctly set/maintained. This is a specific missing-test gap for newly added nontrivial error-handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:222 — badPasswordHandler now reads the auth note directly instead of calling the overridable isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(), so subclasses that override that hook get a form state that no longer matches their user-resolution logic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `badPasswordHandler` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` replacing `if (isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)) { ... }` with `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context);`. The new utility method reads the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` directly from the authentication session, bypassing the previously-called `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)` hook. If subclasses override that method to customize the “user already set” determination, this change could alter form state behavior for those subclasses. The diff doesn’t prove any such overrides exist or that it breaks runtime behavior in this PR, but it is a concrete extensibility/architecture concern introduced by the change.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 — No check that the identified user actually has a passkey credential, so re-auth users without passkeys get passkey UI and UsernameForm stops auto-skipping for them whenever realm passkeys are enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows conditional-passkeys setup in `UsernamePasswordForm` is now gated only by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` (webauthnAuth!=null, realm passkeys enabled, and user!=null) with no check that the identified user actually has any WebAuthn/passwordless credentials (`UsernamePasswordForm.java` adds `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` and calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` whenever it returns true). Also `UsernameForm.authenticate` now refuses to auto-skip when `context.getUser()!=null` if `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true, which can force showing the username step during re-auth whenever conditional passkeys are enabled, regardless of the user’s credentials. However, the diff does not fully prove that a “passkey UI” is rendered for users without passkeys (that depends on what `fillContextForm`/templates do when no authenticators exist, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` to false), so it’s a concrete edge-case concern but not a verified defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:378 — After a failed re-auth attempt the tests only check the error text and never assert the username is hidden (attempted username shown / username input absent) or that registration is disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:294 — try/catch(Exception) around findElement swallows any WebDriverException, so the "no webauthn form" check can pass without really checking; use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as the other tests do.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the diff adds checks like `try { driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")) ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }`. Catching `Exception` will treat any WebDriver/runtime failure (e.g., StaleElementReferenceException, invalid session, other WebDriverException) as “expected”, so the test can pass without actually verifying the element is absent. Using `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` (as other tests in this diff do) would make the check precise.
